predecessors.name: Kingdom of Spain
predecessors.text: the centre and north of Spain that the French held in 1808: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Spain shape of 1808 minus its 1809 shape

successors.name: Kingdom of Spain
successors.text: the Spain restored to Ferdinand VII: Vitoria (21 June 1813) and the Treaty of Valençay (8 December 1813)

ledger.x: 15 June 1808: Joseph Bonaparte is made King of Spain.
June 1808: Spain under Joseph is a Napoleonic client state (page: 'a Napoleonic client state that existed from 1808 to 1813').
1 August 1808: after Bailén 'Joseph evacuated the capital for Old Castile' and the French army sheltered behind the Ebro (the Joseph page: he left Madrid in July after Bailén).
1 December 1808: 'Madrid surrendered on 1 December and Joseph Bonaparte was restored to his throne' (the Joseph page: 2 December) after Napoleon's campaign.
1810: 'Biscay, Navarre, and Aragon were military governments dependent on Paris from 1810', and Catalonia too; Catalonia is 'territory annexed to the French Empire' from 1812 (infobox).
19 January 1810: 'The French invaded Andalusia on 19 January 1810' and took most of the south except Cádiz; the Junta dissolved itself on 29 January.
9 January 1812: Suchet takes Valencia: 'on 9 January 1812 after a brief siege'.
11 August 1812: 'King Joseph Bonaparte abandoned Madrid on 11 August' after Salamanca (22 July); Madrid 'surrendered on 14 August' and the siege of Cádiz ended in the retreat.
Late 1812: Joseph is again in Madrid; the page is silent on the return and the date is inferred from his leaving Madrid again on 17 March 1813.
17 March 1813: Joseph leaves Madrid for the last time ('on 17 March el rey intruso').
June 1813: Joseph 'permanently left Spain in June'; the client kingdom has no land left.
June 1813: Joseph permanently leaves Spain; the Treaty of Valençay of 8 December 1813 restores Ferdinand VII and the Cortes of Cádiz repudiated it (Treaty page).

wars.name: Peninsular War
wars.outcome: The French invaded in February 1808, Joseph was restored on 1 December 1808, Andalusia fell in January 1810, Valencia in January 1812; Salamanca (22 July 1812) and Vitoria (21 June 1813) ended Joseph's rule.

certainty.note: Occupation fronts moved with every campaign and the pages name cities and provinces only; each extent is a reading anchored on Cliopatria's free-zone shapes of the Kingdom of Spain.
